source.title: Queue mode: Redis pub/sub teardown precedes execution drain; MCP session registration fails during shutdown

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

In queue mode, `Start.stopProcess()` disconnects the shared Redis publisher and subscriber **before** awaiting the final `ActiveExecutions.shutdown()` drain. An observed MCP Server Trigger failure during a prolonged container stop followed the session-registration path into that closed publisher and failed immediately with **"Connection is closed."**

Please investigate the dependency ordering between HTTP/MCP shutdown, active execution draining, and Redis pub/sub teardown. The requested fix is narrowly about shutdown lifecycle correctness, not reconnecting a deliberately stopped client or extending shutdown timeouts.

**Evidence strength:** the ordering and failing stack are confirmed. The production failures occurred inside the old container's stop interval. The old process's logs were no longer retained, so the exact call to `Publisher.shutdown()` at the time of failure was not captured. A complete reproduction on an unmodified official image has not been run.

### Environment

- n8n **2.46.6**, self-hosted Docker Compose, Linux x64.
- Node.js **26.12.1**.
- PostgreSQL and Redis **7.4**, queue mode, one main and five workers.
- MCP Server Trigger: `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.mcpTrigger`, type version **2.1**.
- `EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue`.
- `N8N_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT=900`.
- The deployment uses a derived image carrying upstream PR #42436 (Agent token-counting changes). This is **not** claimed to be a reproduction on the stock image. The relevant ordering was independently checked in the official `n8n@2.46.6` source and matches the installed code.

### Sanitised observed evidence

Relative times below preserve the incident timing while omitting infrastructure and workflow identities.

| Observation | Time from initial host stop event |
| --- | ---: |
| Host Docker daemon records `stopping restart-manager` for the old container | T+0 |
| First retained MCP execution fails | approximately T+517 s |
| Three further MCP executions fail | approximately T+880, T+889 and T+899 s |
| Old container task is deleted/exits | approximately T+902 s |
| Replacement main starts | approximately T+907 s |

The roughly 15-minute stop interval is consistent with the configured 900-second graceful-shutdown timeout; it is **not** proof of which drain operation consumed the interval or whether exit was forced. No old-process shutdown stack or signal-level trace remains.

All four retained executions:
- Had `mode=webhook`, `status=error`.
- Failed in **18–38 ms**.
- Belonged to the same MCP-trigger workflow.
- Failed at the trigger/session setup stage. The selected error was not a downstream tool failure.

Selected error stack, with installation prefixes and dependency versions removed:

```text
Error: Connection is closed.
    at EventEmitter.sendCommand (ioredis/built/Redis.js:332:28)
    at EventEmitter.set (ioredis/built/utils/Commander.js:90:25)
    at Publisher.set (packages/cli/src/scaling/pubsub/publisher.service.ts:129:21)
    at Object.set (packages/cli/src/scaling/scaling.service.ts:158:53)
    at RedisSessionStore.register (.../McpTrigger/session/RedisSessionStore.ts:21:24)
    at SessionManager.registerSession (.../McpTrigger/session/SessionManager.ts:27:20)
    at McpServer.setupSession (.../McpTrigger/McpServer.ts:485:29)
    at McpServer.handleSetupRequest (.../McpTrigger/McpServer.ts:123:14)
    at McpTrigger.webhook (.../McpTrigger/McpTrigger.node.ts:330:20)
```

Redis's container had not restarted across the incident. A later check returned `PONG`; cumulative Redis counters showed zero rejected connections, evicted clients, and output-buffer-limit disconnections. These checks do not establish uninterrupted network availability at every instant, but the selected stack specifically shows use of an ended client rather than a Redis command rejection.

There are no later retained calls to this workflow after replacement, so restart recovery of this MCP endpoint has **not** been demonstrated.

### Confirmed source path

The official [2.46.6 Start.stopProcess implementation](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.46.6/packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts#L89-L119) performs pub/sub teardown ahead of the final active-execution wait. This dependency order also appears in the installed compiled code.

`Publisher.shutdown()` calls its client's `disconnect()`. `ScalingService.setupQueue()` gives `RedisSessionStore` functions backed by this same publisher; session registration calls its `set()`.

HTTP shutdown needs to be considered with that ordering. [AbstractServer.onShutdown](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%402.46.6/packages/cli/src/abstract-server.ts) invokes `server.close(callback)` but returns without awaiting callback completion. `BaseCommand.onTerminationSignal()` awaits shutdown hooks before calling `stopProcess()`. Merely invoking server close is not an awaited proof that all outstanding HTTP/MCP work has settled.

This does **not** claim that the listener keeps accepting arbitrary new TCP connections after `server.close()`. The regression investigation should distinguish existing requests/sessions, deferred callbacks and new admission.

### Minimal component check actually run

Using the installed ioredis **5.3.2**, an isolated lazy client with no connection initiated:

```js
const client = new Redis({
  lazyConnect: true,
  host: '127.0.0.1',
  port: 1,
});
client.disconnect();

try {
  await client.set('synthetic-diagnostic-key', 'x');
} catch (error) {
  console.log(client.status, error.message);
}
// end Connection is closed.
```

This reproduced the exact closed-client error without connecting to production Redis or executing a workflow. It demonstrates the client-state behaviour only; it is **not** a full n8n shutdown reproduction.

### Reproduction to add / verify

In an isolated queue-mode fixture with PostgreSQL, Redis, main and a worker:

1. Publish a minimal MCP Server Trigger workflow with a harmless tool, and establish the supported MCP connection/session.
2. Keep controlled MCP/execution work outstanding so main has work to drain.
3. Signal main to shut down while Redis remains available.
4. Use barriers around HTTP/MCP close completion and active-execution settlement to exercise session-registration/cleanup callbacks during shutdown.
5. Trace publisher/subscriber disconnect calls and MCP/queue operations. Verify whether required Redis work can occur after disconnect.
6. Check graceful completion and bounded cancellation separately. Test official 2.46.6 first, then the proposed fix.

Those full integration steps are proposed regression work, not steps claimed to have been executed against production.

### Expected behaviour / scope

- Stop admitting new MCP work once shutdown begins, and settle or deliberately cancel outstanding requests/sessions within the existing shutdown budget.
- Keep shared Redis dependencies available for all work the shutdown path still permits or awaits.
- Disconnect pub/sub only after its consumers have settled, or establish an explicit safe cancellation boundary before disconnect.
- Do not leave drain logic waiting on completion messages after its subscriber has already been closed.
- Requests affected by intentional shutdown should receive a controlled shutdown outcome rather than an incidental closed-client exception.

Acceptance should cover active MCP sessions, concurrent requests/session registration, a queued tool in flight, no-work shutdown, normal queued webhook completion, Redis genuinely unavailable during shutdown, repeated shutdown signals, and timeout/cancellation paths. Assert dependency ordering and bounded exit with deterministic barriers, not only a sleep-based test.

Keep queue-mode execution semantics and authentication intact. No new settings, background reconnect loop for intentionally stopped clients, increased graceful timeout, or broad MCP redesign is requested. Moving teardown later alone needs verification against all existing shutdown hooks and HTTP close behaviour.

### Related work and limits

Searched upstream issues for MCP + "Connection is closed", shutdown + Redis, and shutdown + publisher; no matching open report was found. Worker dequeue/return fixes such as #40086/#40162 concern a different lifecycle path.

No workflow content, customer/user/workflow/node names, identifiers, hostnames, addresses, credentials, raw inputs/outputs, container IDs or identifying screenshots are included. Investigation was read-only apart from the isolated no-connection component check. No production fix or end-to-end shutdown test is claimed.
